records.abstract_excerpt: Bioactive lipids are low-abundance, rapidly acting signaling molecules that orchestrate vascular homeostasis and remodeling through a closed-loop cycle of synthesis, localization, receptor/effector sensing, and inactivation. records.title: Oxylipins in Atherosclerosis: Their Role in Inflammation, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
records.abstract_excerpt: Atherosclerosis, the principal pathology underlying cardiovascular diseases, is now recognized as a chronic inflammatory disorder of the arterial wall. This review focuses on the central role of oxylipins, a diverse family of bioactive lipids derived from polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), in the inflammatory processes driving atherosclerosis. The enrichment analysis strongly implicates **Eicosanoid synthesis** (Wikipathways WP167, FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment = 1429.66) and **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism** (KEGG map00590) as the top candidate pathways. Five of the seven input metabolites — arachidonic acid (C00219), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — are annotated in these pathways, grounding the finding in high-confidence membership evidence.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid is the primary upstream substrate: KEGG graph analysis confirms it is reachable in 2 hops to both 5-HETE (via C05356, the 5-HPETE intermediate) and to leukotriene A4 (via the same 5-HPETE branch point), establishing it as the likely initiating molecule of the observed eicosanoid cascade. The elevated HETEs and leukotriene A4 in the treatment group are consistent with lipoxygenase-driven oxidation of arachidonic acid, as supported by literature demonstrating that HETEs are oxylipin products of 5- and 15-lipoxygenase acting on arachidonic acid (PMID 41226613). 15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2, a cyclopentenone prostaglandin, is also a downstream product of the same arachidonic acid pool and is a known ligand for PPARγ; together, these five metabolites are all annotated within the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway (Wikipathways WP167), indicating that the treatment activates multiple parallel branches of this pathway.

**Biological significance.** Eicosanoids are potent lipid mediators of inflammation, immune cell chemotaxis, and vascular tone. The coordinated elevation of multiple HETEs and leukotriene A4 points to upregulated 5-lipoxygenase and 15-lipoxygenase activity — a pattern reported in inflammatory disorders, allergic responses, and cardiovascular injury (PMID 41226613). The appearance of losartan, an AT1-receptor antagonist, in the input list is notable because angiotensin II signaling is known to synergize with leukotriene pathways to amplify vascular inflammation and oxidative stress (PMID 41783891); losartan's presence in the list may indicate a treatment arm designed to attenuate this crosstalk.

In summary, the data strongly support **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism** (KEGG map00590) as the central hub, with **arachidonic acid as the verified upstream driver**, and with the collective elevation of 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 all mapped to the **Eicosanoid synthesis** pathway (Wikipathways WP167).

**Limitations.** Pathway enrichment is limited to annotated metabolites present in RaMP/KEGG databases; additional unmeasured eicosanoids may be involved. Causality cannot be inferred from metabolomics data alone and requires experimental validation.
